title: Is Invest In Cryptocurrency Is Safe?
content:
Is Invest In Cryptocurrency Is Safe?


    
Cryptocurrency crimes include hackers stealing coins from investors and people falling for cryptocurrency investment scams. According to a report by Crypto Head, a cryptocurrency news channel that uses data from the Federal Trade Commission to analyze trends in cryptocurrency crime in recent years, reports of crimes against cryptocurrencies increased by an annual average of 31.2% in 2016.
    



Earlier this year, CNBC predicted that the cryptocurrency market could reach $1 trillion by the end of 2018. However, investing is risky, and experts say cryptocurrencies are one of the riskiest investment decisions of all, according to Consumer Reports. Investing in cryptocurrencies is not as complex as investing in equities, but the wealth of stocks available confuses us every day.
    
According to Claire Lovell, Associate Director of Product Management at Gemini, an investment platform for cryptocurrency, Bitcoin has reached an all-time high and traditional financial institutions are adopting cryptocurrency, meaning that digital currencies are becoming an increasingly important part of the financial and fintech industries. As more and more companies and platforms find ways to use cryptocurrencies and let their customers use them, it will become a common cryptocurrency. As for the benefits, Lovell says cryptocurrencies offer consumers greater choice, independence and opportunity in their finances.
    



The high returns of Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies offer investors ease and a greater degree of independence. But, despite their returns, the risks associated with cryptocurrencies far exceed those of any other asset class. Unlike buying and trading commodities in fiat or government-issued currencies, buying bitcoin or any type of cryptocurrency is not without risk.

The volatile price of Bitcoins makes them riskier than shares or other forms of investment, but also more profitable. The nature of Bitcoins as an emerging technology and the knowledge required to purchase and store your Bitcoins increase the risk involved.
    



Despite the increased incidence of fraud and theft, many experts praise Bitcoin's security as an investment, at least in terms of cybersecurity, if not investment stability, thanks to the secure blockchain technology. If you are looking for a safe investment with guaranteed returns, do not invest in bitcoin or cryptocurrencies. Here's what you need to know about the security of Bitcoins as an asset and how to keep your cryptocurrency safe when you invest.
    
It should be noted that investments in cryptocurrencies are legal in India, but there is no law prohibiting individuals from buying and selling virtual coins. There are a few different ways to buy Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, including through exchanges and traditional brokers. In Bitcoin you can start investing using cryptocurrencies like Coinbase and a few traditional brokers like Robinhood.
    


Exploring the cryptocurrency space is not a bad idea for people with a high risk appetite and patience to stay invested for long. People should make sure they do proper research before they invest. It is recommended that you set up an emergency fund to repay high-interest debt before putting money into Bitcoin or any other cryptocurrency.
    
Whether investing in cryptocurrencies is safe remains a hotly debated issue in finance, with many in favor of decentralized digital currencies and just as many against. Average investor Mark Cuban compares Bitcoin to gambling and advises investing as much as he can afford to lose. Because of the high selling price of Bitcoins, you can buy as much as 5% of a Bitcoin, with the option to buy shares called Satoshis, says Anthony Pompliano, co-founder of the Morgan Creek Digital Assets Cryptocurrency Fund and Bitcoin investor.
    


From an investment perspective the risks associated with Bitcoin, Ethereum, Ether and other cryptocurrencies are similar to those associated with other traditional assets, aside from the fact that the virtual coin market is highly volatile. Analysts say cryptocurrencies are risky assets and that wild price swings are common in the virtual coin trade space.
    
While Bitcoin and Ether have gained enormous popularity, other notable cryptocurrencies are regaining in popularity: Litecoin, Polkadot, Cardano and many more. Bitcoin is seen as a trendsetter, and trading in cryptocurrencies has proven to be a major driver of investor interest.
   

If you follow the news, you probably already know a few things about Bitcoin. But if you are like many others, you are uncertain about a number of things, including what a crypto is, how it works, and whether it is a safe way to invest your money.
    
Cryptocurrencies are digital currencies underpinned by distributed ledger technology, which is the most secure technology ever. While Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies may be used in private markets to exchange goods and services, they are not considered legal tender like US dollar coins. Instead, cryptocurrencies serve as a medium of exchange, and they are an asset class that people can trade to make a profit.
    



When you sign up for a cryptocurrency exchange, you can buy, sell or hold cryptocurrencies. To buy Bitcoin you need a digital wallet, a personal identification document, secure internet connection and the cryptocurrency as payment methods.
